entries.title: Day trip to Apollonia and Berat
entries.summary: North to the ruins of ancient Apollonia, then inland to Berat’s Ottoman old town, a UNESCO World Heritage site — a long, rewarding day away from the coast.
keywords: Greek and Roman ruins at Apollonia
Berat’s UNESCO-listed old town and castle
A good plan for a windy day on the coast

entries.title: Dukat: olive groves and a country lunch
entries.summary: Below the Llogara road, the Dukat plain is olive-oil country. Agritourism farms serve local dishes, their own oil and wine — a slow lunch on the way to or from the Riviera.
keywords: Olive oil from the Dukat plain
Easy to combine with the Llogara Pass

entries.title: Evening on the Lungomare
entries.summary: The promenade after dark: the xhiro, the Ferris wheel, dinner by the water and the city lights you see on the night camera.
keywords: The evening walk along the promenade

entries.title: Haxhi Ali Cave by boat
entries.summary: A large sea cave at the northern tip of Karaburun, entered by boat on calm days — one of the most photographed stops on the coast.
keywords: Entering the cave by boat in calm conditions
The sheer cliffs of outer Karaburun
Clear water for swimming near the cave entrance

entries.title: Kanina Castle and the view over the bay
entries.summary: A hilltop castle above the village of Kanina, south-east of the city: Illyrian origins, walls rebuilt by Romans, Byzantines and Ottomans, and the whole bay at your feet.
keywords: Panorama over Vlora, Sazan and Karaburun
Walls and towers spanning Illyrian to Ottoman times

entries.title: Llogara Pass and the Riviera road
entries.summary: The mountain road south of the bay climbs to about 1,000 m through the Llogara pine forest and drops to the Albanian Riviera — a day trip or the start of the next leg.
keywords: Panoramic views over Vlora Bay and the Riviera

entries.title: Lungomare city beaches
entries.summary: The beaches along Vlora’s promenade — walkable from the centre, lined with cafés, and the ones you see on the live camera every day.
keywords: Walk straight from town onto the sand
Sunbeds, showers and cafés in season
Sunset views over Sazan from the promenade

entries.title: Old Beach (Plazhi i Vjetër)
entries.summary: Vlora’s original town beach, on the far side of the port to the north-west — quieter than the Lungomare beaches, with older buildings among newer hotels.
keywords: Wooded shore and camping further north at Boves

entries.title: Old Town, Flag Square and the Muradie Mosque
entries.summary: The historic heart of Vlora: where Albania declared independence in 1912, a 16th-century Ottoman mosque, and the old quarter on the hill.
keywords: Independence Monument in Flag Square; Museum of Independence by the port
Kuzum Baba viewpoint over the city and bay

entries.title: Orikum and the ruins of ancient Oricum
entries.summary: At the southern end of the bay: the small town of Orikum, its lagoon and marina, and the remains of Oricum, the harbour Julius Caesar took in 48 BC.
keywords: Remains of a Greek and Roman harbour town
The bay’s southern beaches and lagoon
Gateway to the Llogara Pass and boats to Karaburun

entries.title: Paragliding over Vlora Bay
entries.summary: Tandem flights from the hills above the bay, landing on the beach — the paragliders you spot on the live camera on suitable days.
keywords: Panorama of the whole bay from the air
No experience needed for tandem flights

entries.title: Private boat charter from Vlora
entries.summary: Your own boat and skipper for a family or group: choose the coves, set the pace, and go as far as Grama Bay on a long day.
keywords: Set your own itinerary and timings
Reach quieter coves away from the shared-boat stops
Ideal for families and groups of 4–10

entries.title: Sazan Island & Karaburun boat trip
entries.summary: The classic Vlora day on the water: across the bay to Albania’s largest island, then along the wild Karaburun coast with swim stops.
keywords: Albania’s largest island and its former military installations
Swim stops in Karaburun coves without road access
Views back across the bay to Vlora and the Lungomare
Often combined with the Haxhi Ali sea cave

entries.title: Seafood lunch on the waterfront
entries.summary: Grilled fish, mussels from the lagoon and a long table by the water: the Vlora lunch that works in any weather.
keywords: Tables by the water along the Lungomare
An indoor plan for windy or wet days

entries.title: Snorkelling along the Karaburun coast
entries.summary: Clear water, sea caves and rocky coves inside the Karaburun-Sazan marine park, reached on boat trips that build in swim and snorkel stops.
keywords: Deep, clear water under limestone cliffs
Swim stops near sea caves and coves

entries.title: Sunset cruise on Vlora Bay
entries.summary: Leave the waterfront in the last two hours of light and watch the sun drop behind Sazan Island from the water.
keywords: Sunset behind Sazan Island from the water
City lights coming on along the Lungomare
Short, low-commitment outing with no swimming required

entries.title: Tandem paragliding from the Llogara Pass
entries.summary: Take off from the mountains by the Llogara Pass, about a thousand metres up, and glide down towards the Ionian coast — the Riviera alternative to the bay flight.
keywords: Launch high above the Ionian coast
Pine forest and mountain views at the pass
Combine with a day on the Riviera beaches

entries.title: Zvërnec monastery and the Narta Lagoon
entries.summary: A wooden footbridge to a pine-covered islet with a medieval monastery, in a lagoon where flamingos winter — twenty minutes north of the city.
keywords: Footbridge walk to the monastery islet
Flamingos and wetland birds in the lagoon
Quiet beach and dunes on the sea side

entries.title: Haxhi Ali Cave
entries.summary: A high sea cave at the northern tip of Karaburun that boats can enter on calm days; a highlight of most coastal boat trips.

entries.title: Karaburun Peninsula
entries.summary: The wild, roadless mountain arm that forms the western side of Vlora Bay — caves, coves and beaches reached only by boat or on foot.

entries.title: Lungomare
entries.summary: Vlora’s waterfront promenade and city beaches — cafés, palms, the pier and the Ferris wheel — and the camera’s most frequent subject.

entries.title: Old Beach (Plazhi i Vjetër)
entries.summary: Vlora’s original town beach, north-west of the port and away from the Lungomare promenade: quieter, with older buildings among newer hotels.

entries.title: Port of Vlora
entries.summary: The ferry and cargo port at the north end of the Lungomare, west of the centre, where the Brindisi ferries berth and working boats come and go through the day.

entries.title: Sazan Island
entries.summary: Albania’s largest island, a former military base at the mouth of the bay and the silhouette on the horizon in almost every camera view.

entries.title: Zvërnec and the Narta Lagoon
entries.summary: A monastery islet reached by footbridge in a shallow lagoon north of the city, with salt pans, dunes and wintering flamingos.

entries.title: Eden by Valza
entries.summary: The rooftop restaurant of the Valza Boutique Hotel at Uji i Ftohtë: modern Albanian and Mediterranean cooking and Albanian wines, looking out over the bay.
keywords: Uji i Ftohtë, on the coast road south of the centre

entries.title: Paradise Beach Restaurant
entries.summary: A Mediterranean and Italian restaurant on the beach side of the Lungomare; the menu centres on local seafood, with a raw-fish bar and dry-aged steaks.
keywords: Lungomare (Rruga Murat Tërbaçi), on the beach

entries.title: Taverna Te Lilo
entries.summary: A taverna whose menu is built around traditional Albanian dishes, with seafood, pasta and risotto alongside — and breakfast from the morning.
keywords: By the port, near Independence Square (Sheshi i Pavarësisë)

entries.title: Oazi Blu Diving Center
entries.summary: Dive centre in Vlora teaching PADI and SSI courses and running boat dives to the Karaburun coast, Sazan and a wreck in Vlora Bay.
keywords: Vlora; summer meeting points also at Jala and Palasa beaches

entries.title: Scuba.al
entries.summary: Vlora dive centre offering shore and boat dives, night dives, Karaburun trips and SDI training from Open Water to Rescue Diver and Nitrox.

entries.title: Hotel Nimfa
entries.summary: A beachfront hotel on the coast south of Vlora with its own beach, sea-view balconies in most rooms, a restaurant and a beach bar.
keywords: South coast road, beyond Uji i Ftohtë

entries.title: Hotel Vlora International
entries.summary: A city hotel where the main boulevard meets the Lungomare by the port, with rooms facing the coast or the promenade, an indoor pool and a spa.
keywords: Port end of the Lungomare (Sheshi Isa Boletini, Rruga Çamëria)

entries.title: Sea & Sand Hotel
entries.summary: A beach hotel a few steps from the Old Beach (Plazhi i Vjetër), with sea-view and family rooms, a restaurant, a garden and free parking.
keywords: Old Beach, north-west of the port (Rruga Sazani)

entries.title: Flag and Independence Day
entries.summary: The anniversary of Albania’s declaration of independence, made in Vlora on 28 November 1912. A national holiday; in 2026 the day off moves to Monday 30 November.

entries.title: Airport transfers
entries.summary: Tirana airport to Vlorë: the official airport bus timetable, fixed taxi fares and private transfers.
keywords: How do I get from Tirana airport to Vlora?

answer.label: Airport bus
answer.note: Nine departures a day each way on the airport’s timetable. From the airport: 03:30, 11:00, 12:30, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00, 20:00, 22:15 and 00:45. From Vlorë: 01:30, 03:30, 06:00, 07:00, 09:00, 11:00, 13:00, 15:00 and 20:00.

answer.label: Airport taxi
answer.note: Published by the airport taxi service; the destination card and fare list differ by €5. Payable in lek, euro or by card.
